title: Taiwan eyes silicon photonics as next big tech leap
gist: Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs is positioning the island to dominate co-packaged optics (CPO) and silicon photonics manufacturing, citing Nvidia's $4 billion March investment in the technology and Taiwan's existing >90% share of advanced (7nm and below) chip capacity and majority share of global OSAT, with a government-backed Silicon Photonics Industry Alliance of 30+ companies formed in 2024.

themes.theme: Silicon photonics as the answer to AI's bandwidth bottleneck

insights.claim: Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs frames silicon photonics as an emerging mainstream optical communications technology that is key to overcoming bottlenecks in AI computing power.
insights.speaker: Ministry of Economic Affairs (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: Government-level framing of photonics as an AI-bottleneck solution signals coordinated industrial policy support (subsidies, R&D programs) is likely to keep flowing to the sector, reducing execution risk for participants.
insights.locator: opening paragraphs on silicon photonics rationale

insights.claim: Silicon photonics replaces copper-wire electronic signal transmission between chips with optical signals; because light generates almost no heat during transmission, the technology can reduce power consumption by 30 to 50 percent.
insights.speaker: Ministry of Economic Affairs (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A 30-50% power-consumption reduction claim gives investors a concrete efficiency metric to model into AI datacenter TCO improvements once CPO is deployed at scale.

insights.claim: Co-packaged optics (CPO) is aimed at overcoming the 1.6-terabit-per-second bandwidth limit of traditional electronic transmission.
insights.speaker: Ministry of Economic Affairs (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A specific 1.6 Tbps ceiling on electronic interconnect gives a hard technical trigger point for when hyperscalers/AI accelerator vendors must transition to optical I/O, useful for timing photonics-supplier revenue inflection.

insights.claim: Nvidia invested US$4 billion in silicon photonics technology in March, according to Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs.
insights.speaker: Ministry of Economic Affairs (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A $4 billion Nvidia commitment to photonics is a direct signal that the largest AI compute buyer sees optical interconnect as a near-term scaling requirement, likely pulling forward capex for photonics-capable packaging/foundry partners.

themes.theme: Taiwan's structural advantages and alliance strategy

insights.claim: Taiwan accounts for more than half of the global outsourced semiconductor assembly and testing (OSAT) market and holds more than 90 percent of global advanced semiconductor manufacturing capacity for 7 nanometer chips or below, which the government says positions it well for CPO and silicon photonics manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Ministry of Economic Affairs (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: Combining majority OSAT share with near-monopoly advanced-node capacity gives Taiwan a structural moat in CPO manufacturing that is difficult for other regions (US, EU, Japan) to replicate quickly, reinforcing Taiwan-concentration risk/reward in AI supply chains.
insights.locator: paragraph on Taiwan's OSAT and advanced-node share

insights.claim: Silicon photonics is a key project under Taiwan's government New 10 Major AI Infrastructure Projects, with a dedicated R&D initiative launched this year under the A+ Enterprise Innovation R&D Program to support development of key technologies.
insights.speaker: Ministry of Economic Affairs (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: Explicit inclusion in a named national infrastructure program indicates sustained multi-year state funding rather than a one-off grant, a positive signal for the durability of Taiwan's photonics push.
insights.locator: paragraph on the New 10 Major AI Infrastructure Projects

insights.claim: The Ministry of Economic Affairs and SEMI helped more than 30 leading companies, including TSMC, ASE Technology Holding, MediaTek and Hon Hai Precision Industry, establish the Silicon Photonics Industry Alliance in 2024, aimed at overcoming key technological hurdles (particularly in CPO) and ensuring Taiwan retains control of the supply chain.
insights.speaker: Ministry of Economic Affairs (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A 30+ company alliance spanning foundry (TSMC), OSAT (ASE), fabless (MediaTek) and EMS (Hon Hai) indicates vertically coordinated industrial policy explicitly designed to keep photonics IP and manufacturing onshore — a supply-chain-control thesis investors should track for potential export-control or geopolitical friction.
insights.locator: final paragraphs on the Silicon Photonics Industry Alliance
